notes:
Summary: mid/large ecommerce support org; focusing on agent-facing RAG for ticket deflection + suggested replies. Primary pain: high cost per support ticket and long handle times. Want top-5 answer quality reliably and tight latency for agent UX. Two-stage architecture preferred: ANN embeddings -> cross-encoder rerank for top-5.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2026-01-08: Inbound lead from tech blog, AE outreach (Maya). initial discovery call scheduled.
- 2026-01-19: Discovery call (30m) w/ Head of Support (L. Martinez) + Eng mgr (S. Chen). Recorded (ff_2026-02-19_7821). Notes: "we need answers now — agents can't wait >300ms for suggestions".
- 2026-02-01: Demo of Redwood hosted API for embeddings + reranking (AE + SE). Follow-up doc with latency tradeoffs shared.
- 2026-02-19: Deep tech session w/ SE Jordan Li, discussed two-stage rerank, vector index sharding, cold-start cache. Action: provide latency baseline on 100M doc subset.
- 2026-03-03: Security kickoff + questionnaire delivered; Fireflies call (ff_2026-03-03_9920). InfoSec asked for SOC2 + KMS integration details.
- 2026-03-09: Pre-POC sync — confirmed POC dataset (historical tickets, KB articles, product docs ~250M passages after chunking).

Technical requirements / acceptance criteria (customer):
- Indexing scale: target ~200M-300M passages, average passage size 400 tokens, expect index growth 20%/quarter. Must support incremental indexing.
- Latency SLOs: end-to-end top-5 rerank 95th <120ms, 99th <200ms for agent UI under expected peak 200 qps (burst to 500 qps). Agent UX is very sensitive to tail latency.
- Throughput: baseline 200 qps sustained during business hours; 1K qps burst capability desirable.
- Quality: reranker must improve MRR for top-5 vs baseline ANN-only by +12-18% on held-out eval sets.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost per query (end-to-end) < $0.015 avg at baseline; procurement team will run TCO against current vendor spend.
- Model preferences: flexible to use open embedding models (e.g., text-embedding-ada alternatives) but want Redwood recommendations for quantized cross-encoder variants for rerank.
- Routing/fallback: multi-tier routing — primary dedicated pool in NA, fallback hosted tier in case of capacity. Must preserve data residency and KMS envelope encryption for fallback logs.
- Observability: token-level cost + per-route latency breakdowns + retrain/regression alerts tied to evaluation prompts.

POC plan (2 weeks):
- Week 0: dataset ingestion (ETL), sample index (100M passages) + baseline ANN retrieval (Pinecone/FAISS) to compare.
- Week 1: Redwood embeddings + ANN -> measure recall@100 and candidate latency. Deploy cross-encoder reranker on dedicated pool (small scale) and measure top-5 latency distribution.
- Week 2: Scale to 250M passages, run synthetic agent load at 200 qps and 500 qps burst, produce cost per-query analysis and quality metrics (MRR, top-5 P@5). Deliver final report + exec summary.

Procurement / legal notes:
- InfoSec requires SOC2 Type II report and evidence of KMS integration. NDA executed 2026-02-25.
- Data residency: customer requires logs/use metadata stored in NA only. Discussed VPC/private deployment options; they favor Dedicated (reserved pool) if cost + latency align.

Quotes / direct lines from stakeholders:
- L. Martinez (Head of Support): "If we can't get suggestions in <250ms the agents will ignore them — so tail matters more than median."
- S. Chen (Eng): "We want the reranker to catch the edge cases where embedding recall pulls noisy docs; top-5 must be precise."

Open action items:
- Provide 95th/99th percentile latency measurements on 100M subset (SE - Jordan) by 2026-03-14.
- Share detailed cost model with Reserved vs Hosted for expected QPS (Finance).
- Complete InfoSec questionnaire answers and provide SOC2 artifact (Security).
- Schedule procurement deep-dive during week of 2026-04-06.

Next step (short): schedule POC kick-off, finalize SOW, and sign test data access agreement.

Stability / notes: customer is pragmatic, heavy ops-minded. Strong chance to convert if POC proves tail latency and cost targets. Keep communications technical and include concrete latency/cost numbers.
